question: Coulomb/second is a unit of which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ELECTRIC CURRENT

 
 
• The flow of electric charge per unit of time is known as electric current
 
• If one coulomb of charge crosses an area in one second, then the current thought of that area is one Ampere(A) 
 
• SI unit of current is Ampere (A) or coulomb per second 
 
• Where I is Electric current, Q is electric charge and T is time
 
• Electric current is a scalar quantity
 
• Although, Electric current has both magnitude and direction yet it is a scalar quantity. This is because the law of ordinary Algebra is used to add electric current and the law of vector addition is not applicable to the addition of electricity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Capacitance

 
 
• ​ The capacitance is the capacity of the capacitor to store charge in it. Two conductors are separated by an insinuator (dielectric) and when an electric field is applied, electrical energy is stored in it as a charge.
 
• The capacitance of a capacitor (C): The capacitance of a conductor is the ratio of charge (Q) to it by a rise in its potential (V), i.e.
 
• C = Q/V
 
• The unit of capacitance is the farad, (symbol F ).
 
• Farad is a large unit so generally, we use μF.
 
 
 
• **Resistance**
 
 
• The resistance of a metal rod depends on the resistivity of the **material**, **length**, and **temperature**.
 
• Resistance is the measure of the opposition to the flow of current in an electrical circuit.
 
• Resistance is measured in ohms, and it is denoted by the Greek letter omega (Ω).
 
• **V= IR**
 
 
 
• **​Magnetism**
 
 
• **​**Magnetism is a concept of the** fundamental interactions **in nature, the** interaction between moving charges**.
 
• Like **gravitational force** and **electrostatic force**, the **magnetic force** is an interaction at a distance.
